Neither log carries a header naming the revision, tree or command that produced it - both are bare output lines - and no script in the reviewed changed_paths produced them, so neither log contains what is needed to tell which input was measured. I re-instrumented _expand_spline_saddle_wedges myself and reproduced the 0-call claim (calls=0), which shows the claim is true and that its delivered record is merely unverifiable in place. A header line naming the commit and the command, and committing the small instrument, would close the gap.

justifications.durability: The census driver, its positive control and the receipt are all committed, and re-running the driver regenerates the receipt from the same arithmetic; I re-ran the control and the driver and got the recorded numbers. Held from full because the wedge instrumentation that produced the 0-call and wedge-arithmetic claims is not delivered (no committed script, no header on its logs), and no automated guard pins the retirement decision against a later change reintroducing the wiring.
justifications.evidence: The result is independently reproducible and I reproduced it. refusal_detector_control.py at head prints forced_bound_refused_cell_count 38, true_bound_refused_cell_count 0, realised_maximum_vertex_count 134, and names the same 38 refused cells at forced bound 100; a control that forces a known refusal and shows the detector naming it is exactly the instrument an absence claim needs. The census numbers reproduce exactly through floor._build over the reviewed code: at 110/300/1000 cells, realised max 134, bound 162/154/148, refused 0, included 86/212/652, straight 34/26/20. The build path reaches operator._profile_support (scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py:1039) with no level_run_count, so it is the production support builder the wiring edits, not a side path. Held below full because the two logs cited as evidence for the saddle-wedge claims (saddle-wedge-arithmetic.log and wedge-instrumentation.log) carry no provenance header and the instrumenting code that produced them is not committed, so those claims are not reproducible from the delivered record alone.
justifications.fit: The change sits in the docs/figures receipt tree it maintains, reuses the moment-floor builder and the committed clip, and ships one census driver plus a positive control and a build-evidence fragment. The commit subject is conventional and carries a body; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no AI attribution appears in the commit message or the new source. Symbols and docstrings state mechanism; the only version-looking tokens are the schema ids nova.exact-clip-one-arc-census.v1, which are wire-format identifiers rather than plan labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Section 5's done-when is met end to end: one_arc_census.py runs the diverted analytic certificate row at 110, 300 and 1000 requested cells under the one-arc bound (traced_polygon_vertex_capacity at its one-run default), and one receipt under capacity/one-arc-census/ records per row the realised maximum live vertex count (134 at every count), the bound (162/154/148 = 128 + straight 34/26/20) and the refused-cell count (0), and states the Section 5 verdict that retires the held two-run wiring 61b291089 with the receipt as its evidence. The census reaches the production operator._profile_support (the method the held wiring edits) through the moment-floor builder, so it measures the layout the wiring would widen. Held from full because the retirement rests on one geometry at three resolutions: the analytic bank carries exactly one diverted row (exact_clip_moment_floor.py:78 CASES) and no double-null diverted case, which the receipt states explicitly. Section 5 allows this ('wherever the bank carries them'), so the coverage is compliant, but it is thin.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff base..head is seven files, 426 insertions, 0 deletions, every path inside a declared write path (docs/figures/exact-clip-moment-quadrature/capacity/one-arc-census/ and docs/evidence/fragments/exact-clip-moment-quadrature/). No module, no test and no plan HTML is touched: nova/ and benchmarks/ are byte-identical base..head, so the census runs against unchanged production code. The diff is purely additive.

notes: The reviewed node is a documentation/receipt change with no code arm: it censuses the diverted analytic certificate row against the one-arc bound at three cell counts and, finding no refused cell, retires the held two-run wiring. The substance is sound and independently verified: the census numbers reproduce exactly (134 vs 162/154/148, refused 0), the positive control fires (38 refused cells at forced bound 100, 0 at the true bound), the build reaches the production _profile_support, and the 0-wedge-call claim reproduces under independent instrumentation.
